tips.title: CRITICAL: Okuma G71/G72 are THREADING cycles, not roughing
tips.body: On Okuma OSP, G71 is THREADING COMPOUND CYCLE (longitudinal) and G72 is THREADING COMPOUND CYCLE (transverse). This is the OPPOSITE of Fanuc where G71/G72 are stock removal roughing. Direct post-processor conflict — verify controller before outputting G71/G72.

tips.title: Okuma G31/G32/G33 are single-pass thread cutting cycles
tips.body: G31=longitudinal threading, G32=end face threading, G33=general threading. These are FIXED cycles for single-pass thread cutting. Use G71/G72 for multi-pass compound threading with automatic depth control.

tips.title: Okuma threading M-codes: M22/M23 chamfer, M26/M27 lead direction
tips.body: M22=chamfering OFF, M23=chamfering ON. M26=thread lead along Z-axis, M27=thread lead along X-axis. Infeed patterns: M32 (straight), M33 (zigzag), M34 (straight reversed). Thread cutting patterns: M73/M74/M75.

tips.title: Okuma G73/G74 are GROOVING cycles, not pattern repeat/peck drill
tips.body: G73=Longitudinal Grooving Compound Fixed Cycle, G74=Transverse Grooving Compound Fixed Cycle. On Fanuc, G73=pattern repeat and G74=peck drilling. Another critical G-code conflict requiring post-processor attention.

tips.title: Okuma G75/G76 are chamfering/rounding, not grooving/threading
tips.body: G75=Automatic Chamfering, G76=Automatic Rounding. On Fanuc, G75=grooving and G76=threading. CRITICAL conflict — never output Fanuc G76 threading to Okuma controller.

tips.title: Okuma thread cutting cannot execute in G96 CSS mode
tips.body: Threading operations require G97 constant RPM mode. G96 (constant surface speed) is not valid during thread cutting. Feedrate override is also inoperative during thread cutting — program must run at 100%.

tips.title: Okuma G71 threading format with full parameters
tips.body: G71 X__ Z__ {I__ | A__} B__ D__ U__ H__ L__ E__ F__ J__ M__ Q__. X=final diameter, Z=end point, I=taper radius OR A=taper angle, B=infeed angle, D=first cut depth, U=finish allowance, H=thread height, L=chamfer distance, F=lead, J=threads per lead, Q=number of passes.

tips.title: Okuma M138/M139 SSV for chatter suppression
tips.body: M694=Spindle Speed Variation OFF, M695=Spindle Speed Variation ON. SSV continuously varies spindle RPM within a range to break up chatter harmonics. Use on long cuts or when chatter develops.

tips.title: Okuma G199/G198 spindle synchronization for dual-spindle
tips.body: G199=Synchronize spindles (both at same RPM), G198=Release sync. G96 CSS is blocked during sync mode — use stepped G97 RPM commands instead. Critical for dual-spindle cutoff operations.

tips.title: Okuma incomplete thread length calculation
tips.body: Delta > K × N × P where N=spindle RPM, P=thread lead (mm), K=machine constant (0.48-2.56 × 10^-3). Account for this when programming thread runout zones to prevent collisions.
